readback.name: Poincare.BufferedTensorGraphTransport.weight_zero_off_coordSupport
readback.mathematical_statement: Let E3 be EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), the real three-dimensional Euclidean vector space. For every universe u, let M : Type u have a topology, an E3 charted-space structure, and the C-infinity IsManifold structure for the boundaryless closedSmoothModelWithCorners 3. Let A : AtlasData M. The atlas data includes finitely many genuine extended charts C_k at anchors a_k, open regions covering M with their closures in the corresponding chart sources and compact coordinate images, and a smooth partition of unity p_k on M subordinate to those regions. No Hausdorff, CompactSpace, connectedness, metric, or time typeclass or variable is explicitly assumed in these declarations. Let i index one chart, theta,xi : E3 -> R be total scalar functions, F : E3 -> E3 a total map, and a,b,c,d : Fin 3 coordinate indices. The pinned weight is W(z) = theta(z) * (p_i(C_i.symm(z)) * xi(F(z)) * (DF_z(e_c))_a * (DF_z(e_d))_b), where e_c and e_d are the EuclideanSpace.basisFun vectors and DF_z = fderiv R F z. All factors are real numbers and the products are ordinary real multiplication. The derivatives are actual Frechet derivatives of F; there is no matrix inverse or pointwise reciprocal. Assume only that the topological support of theta is contained in the actual chart target of C_i. Then for every z in E3 outside coordSupport A i, one has W(z) = 0. The pinned coordSupport is C_i image tsupport(p_i). This zero assertion covers every ambient coordinate z, including points outside the target of C_i; no inverse-chart validity is silently assumed there. No global smoothness, compact support, range condition, cutoff-one condition, chart-agreement premise, or regularity of theta, xi, or F is required beyond the stated support inclusion. The claim is pointwise vanishing outside coordSupport, and does not itself state a topological-support subset or norm estimate. There are no time or Hoelder-exponent variables.

readback.name: Poincare.BufferedTensorGraphTransport.weight_pullback_chart
readback.mathematical_statement: Let E3 be EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), the real three-dimensional Euclidean vector space. For every universe u, let M : Type u have a topology, an E3 charted-space structure, and the C-infinity IsManifold structure for the boundaryless closedSmoothModelWithCorners 3. Let A : AtlasData M. The atlas data includes finitely many genuine extended charts C_k at anchors a_k, open regions covering M with their closures in the corresponding chart sources and compact coordinate images, and a smooth partition of unity p_k on M subordinate to those regions. No Hausdorff, CompactSpace, connectedness, metric, or time typeclass or variable is explicitly assumed in these declarations. Let i index one chart, theta,xi : E3 -> R be total scalar functions, F : E3 -> E3 a total map, and a,b,c,d : Fin 3 coordinate indices. The pinned weight is W(z) = theta(z) * (p_i(C_i.symm(z)) * xi(F(z)) * (DF_z(e_c))_a * (DF_z(e_d))_b), where e_c and e_d are the EuclideanSpace.basisFun vectors and DF_z = fderiv R F z. All factors are real numbers and the products are ordinary real multiplication. The derivatives are actual Frechet derivatives of F; there is no matrix inverse or pointwise reciprocal. Let j be another chart index and write T_ij(z) = C_j(C_i.symm(z)), the pinned change A i j. This maps i coordinates to j coordinates. Assume that tsupport(theta) lies in source(C_i.symm.trans C_j), so a supported z is in target(C_i) and C_i.symm(z) is in source(C_j). Assume also that, at every point z in tsupport(theta), F agrees with T_ij on a full ambient E3 neighborhood of z. This is a germ equality using nhds z, rather than equality only at z or on the closed support. Finally, let K_ij = C_i image (tsupport(p_i) intersect (C_j.symm image tsupport(xi))) and assume merely theta(z) = 1 for all z in K_ij. This last premise is pointwise equality, not a cutoff-one germ premise. Then for every arbitrary total scalar function f : E3 -> R and every x in source(C_i), W(C_i(x)) * f(F(C_i(x))) equals p_i(x) times the following piecewise expression: if x is in source(C_j), the expression is xi(C_j(x)) * J_ij(x)_(a,c) * J_ij(x)_(b,d) * f(C_j(x)); if x is not in source(C_j), it is zero. Here J_ij(x)_(a,c) is exactly jac A i j x a c = (D(T_ij) at C_i(x), applied to e_c)_a. Thus a,b are output indices in j coordinates and c,d are input indices in i coordinates. In the source-to-destination tensor-entry interpretation, the source field is in chart j and the destination field in chart i; the map pulls the source argument back along the i-to-j coordinate transition. The right-hand side contains the destination partition p_i and an explicit indicator of source-chart membership, with no p_j factor. The revised @ite with Classical.propDecidable selects this same real-valued piecewise expression; it adds no mathematical assumption or alternative source gate. No smoothness or compact-support hypotheses on theta, xi, F, or f are required in this declaration. No range bound on either scalar function or target-support condition on xi is assumed. The formula includes the off-source-j case explicitly, but is asserted only for x in source(C_i). There are no time variables, Hoelder exponents, Graph identities, operator norms, or tensor compatibility conclusions.
